AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 3, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING - 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

ROLL CALL
   Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor Arthur McKibben
  Norwalk Nazarene Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Ameni Serrano,
  Norwalk Teen Alliance Program Volunteer

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize Hometown Heroes.

  II.  City Council to recognize Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District Students for their internships for
  Liberty Utilities.

  III.  City Council to present a Business Spotlight to Chick-fil-A.

  IV.  City Council to recognize Cerritos College for being named America’s Best Two-Year College Radio
  Station.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  Senior Thanksgiving Luncheon highlights.

  2.  Chamber of Commerce Quarterly Update.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.
   1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  November 16 and 19, 2019. 825-04

  Report

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period October 20, 2019 –
  November 2, 2019, in the total amount of $963,036.25. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  November 14 – November 26, 2019, in the total amount of $3,122,692.52. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Edwin
  Trucking, Inc. (Cristina Macedo and Yeffri-Rivera) and Rene Villanueva Trujillo. 830-04/20

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – NOVEMBER 20, 2019 - No action is required. 320

  Report

  6.  ORDINANCE NO. 19-1711 - ADOPTING TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 319 AMENDING THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH A LIVE-WORK OVERLAY ZONE AND REGULATIONS FOR THE
  SAME AND ORDINANCE NO. 19-1712 - ADOPTING ZONE CHANGE NO. 357 FOR 12038 OLIVE
  STREET, 13211-13253 SAN ANTONIO DRIVE, AND 12027-12033 SPROUL STREET - Staff
  recommends City Council accept for second reading and adopt:

  a.  Ordinance No. 19-1711, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING TITLE 17 OF
  THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH LIVE-WORK OVERLAY ZONE AND
  REGULATIONS FOR THE LIVE-WORK OVERLAY ZONE; and

  b.  Ordinance No. 19-1712, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK SETTING FORTH ITS
  FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION APPROVING ZONE CHANGE NO. 357.

  Report

  7.  PASSPORT ACCEPTANCE AND AGENT CERTIFICATION PAY - Staff recommends City Council
  approve certification pay to the individuals who will issue passports equal to the amount provided for in
  the Memorandum of Understanding between the City and the Norwalk City Employees Association.

  Report

  8.  SPECIAL EVENT REQUEST TO USE CIVIC CENTER LAWN AND PARKING LOT FOR FOOD
  BASKET GIVEAWAY - Staff recommends City Council approve the event requested by the Norwalk
  Float Foundation for Sunday, December 15, 2019 and waive security deposit consistent with past
  practice.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  9.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200 HEARING

  Report

HEARING

  10. HEARING - RESOLUTION NO. 19-60 - APPEAL OF PROPERTY MAINTENANCE AND BUILDING
  REHABILITATION APPEALS BOARD DECISION RELATIVE TO DECLARATION AND ABATEMENT
   OF A PUBLIC NUISANCE - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-60, A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK SETTING FORTH ITS
  FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION RELATIVE TO THE DENIAL OF THE APPEAL AND
  CONFIRMING THE ACTION AND DECISION OF THE PROPERTY MAINTENANCE AND BUILDING
  REHABILITATION APPEALS BOARD RELATIVE TO THE DECLARATION AND ABATEMENT OF A
  PUBLIC NUISANCE AT THE PROPERTY LOCATED AT 12215 SUMMER AVENUE, NORWALK,
  CALIFORNIA - ASSESSOR’S PARCEL NO. 8023-006-014.

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  11. PUBLIC HEARING - ORDINANCE NO. 19-1709 – ADOPTING THE 2019 CALIFORNIA BUILDING,
  RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL, EXISTING BUILDING, AND
  GREEN BUILDING STANDARDS AND AMENDMENTS - AMENDING THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL
  CODE – Staff recommends City Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 19-1709,
  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK ADOPTING BY REFERENCE THE 2019 EDITIONS
  OF THE CALIFORNIA BUILDING, RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL,
  EXISTING BUILDING, AND GREEN BUILDING STANDARDS CODES AND RELATED MODEL
  CODES, WITH APPENDICES AND AMENDMENTS THERETO; AND AMENDING THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE.

  Report

  12. RESOLUTION NO. 19-75 - AMENDING THE CITY OF NORWALK POLICY FOR SMALL WIRELESS
  FACILITIES; AND RESOLUTION NO. 19-76 - AMENDING STANDARD POLE LICENSE AGREEMENT
  FORM TO BE UTILIZED FOR THE INSTALLATION OF A NEW SMALL WIRELESS FACILITY ON
  CITY-OWNED INFRASTRUCTURE - Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 19-75, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AMENDING THE CITY OF NORWALK POLICY FOR SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES; and

  b.  Resolution No. 19-76, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AMENDING STANDARD POLE LICENSE AGREEMENT FORM TO BE UTILIZED FOR THE
  INSTALLATION OF A NEW SMALL WIRELESS FACILITY ON CITY-OWNED
  INFRASTRUCTURE.

  Report

  13. PUBLIC HEARING – ADOPTION OF A NEGATIVE DECLARATION; ADOPTING STREET VACATION
  NO. 88; ADOPTING GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT NO. 182; ADOPTING ZONE CHANGE NO. 361;
  ADOPTING SIGN USE PERMIT NO. 315; ADOPTING A DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT – Staff
  recommends City Council table this matter. REPORT

  Report

REPORTS

  14. RESOLUTION NO. 19-83 - NORWALK ASSOCIATION OF MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING AND RESOLUTION NO. 19-84 - REVISED SALARY
  SCHEDULE – Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 19-83, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPROVING THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AND THE EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT UNIT EMPLOYEES; and

  b.  Resolution No. 19-84, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPROVING THE SALARY SCHEDULE INCORPORATING THE TWO PERCENT COST OF
  LIVING ADJUSTMENT FOR EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT POSITIONS
  EFFECTIVE DECEMBER 29, 2019.

  Report

  15. RESOLUTION NO. 19-85 - REPORTING THE EMPLOYER’S CONTRIBUTION FOR GENERAL UNIT
   EMPLOYEES UNDER THE PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ MEDICAL AND HOSPITAL CARE ACT - Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-85, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK RESCINDING RESOLUTION NO. 18-02, AND FIXING THE EMPLOYER
  CONTRIBUTION AT AN EQUAL AMOUNT FOR EMPLOYEES AND ANNUITANTS UNDER THE
  PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ MEDICAL AND HOSPITAL CARE ACT FOR GENERAL UNIT EMPLOYEES.

  Report

  16. JANUARY MEETING SCHEDULE CONSIDERATION – Staff recommends City Council either:

  a.  cancel the January 7, 2020 meeting and authorize holding one regularly scheduled meeting on
  January 21, 2020, or

  b.  direct staff to take the appropriate steps to move the meetings to January 14 and 28, 2020.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated November 27, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
